html:
The Aka are a forest people of the southwest of the Central African Republic and the north of the Republic of the Congo, known for their complex polyphonic singing, proclaimed by UNESCO a masterpiece of oral heritage in 2003.

They have long lived by hunting with nets and gathering in the rainforest, trading with farming neighbours. Their songs layer many voices and yodelling over one another, with no single leader, and accompany hunts, rites and storytelling.

Recordings of Aka and other forest music by ethnomusicologists influenced composers in Europe and America, among them György Ligeti. Logging and the civil war now threaten the forests where they live, along with the Sango-speaking villages and the related forest peoples further east.
sum: The Aka are a forest people of the southwest of the Central African Republic and the north of the Republic of the Congo, known for their complex polyphonic singing, proclaimed by UNESCO a masterpiece of oral heritage in 2003.
